name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Eric Burlison running with large financial edge
Democrat Missi Hesketh raised only ~$50k with no outside support
model.rationale: Burlison holds a seat with a 21-point Republican lean, has out-raised Hesketh roughly 29-to-1, and faces no outside spending against him, while markets give Democrats only a 3% chance. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from a Safe R rating.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected outside spending surge for Hesketh would be needed to put this on the board.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Missouri's 7th District is one of the most Republican seats in the House, with a 21-point Republican lean. First-term incumbent Eric Burlison is running for reelection and has built a clear financial advantage, raising about $1.5 million and holding nearly $1 million on hand. Democratic challenger Missi Hesketh has raised only about $50,000, and no outside groups are spending in the race. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Burlison roughly a 95% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and district lean all point the same direction, making this a Safe Republican seat with little evidence of competitive risk.
